text:
alice_finleaf: Hey support — we just had a customer-triggered action billed twice. We sent one request to /v1/toolcall, got a 202 Accepted, and later saw two charge events. Repro steps below and logs attached.

sara_support: Sorry about that, alice. Can you paste the original request headers + the service response body you received? Any Idempotency key used?

alice_finleaf: Here is the exact curl we used:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxxx' \\n  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 5e3b2f9a-abc1-4ef0' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"tool":"charge_customer","args":{"customer_id":"CUST-9987","amount":19.99}}' \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/toolcall
```
Response we got: HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
Body: {"status":"accepted","task_id":"t_abc123","request_id":"req-77f"}

devon_platform: Thanks — two quick asks: (1) can you confirm the exact value of the Idempotency-Key that made it to our backend logs? (2) did your client automatically retry on non-2xx or timeout? Important: our async toolcall is accepted-once semantics if the client supplies a stable idempotency key and the call is retried using that same key. If the retry path strips or changes headers, the backend may treat it as a new invocation. :thinking_face:

alice_finleaf: We used the same Idempotency-Key header on our side. From our server logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] outgoing -> POST /v1/toolcall Idempotency-Key=5e3b2f9a req=req-77f
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] received HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted task=t_abc123
[2026-03-15T14:02:18Z] Received webhook: charge_succeeded exec=exec_1 task=t_abc123
[2026-03-15T14:02:19Z] Received webhook: charge_succeeded exec=exec_2 task=t_abc123
```
Two different exec IDs but same task_id and idempotency key.

jamal_sre: That pattern usually indicates a retry/fallback race: either the client retried (creating duplicate requests that lost the idempotency header before hitting the same backend instance) or our gateway retried the request after a transient 504 and forwarded it as a fresh invocation. I pulled the router traces for req-77f: we served a 202 at t=14:02:10, then a follow-up request at t=14:02:17 with no Idempotency-Key header present to the downstream worker, which triggered a second execution.

sara_support: We can see two charge_events in billing for customer CUST-9987: charge_id ch_01 and ch_02. We're going to stop automated refunds until we confirm root cause. We'll open a billing ticket referencing both charge ids — alice, please confirm whether you want us to provision a refund if we confirm duplicate execution.

devon_platform: Immediate mitigation steps we recommend:
- Please disable client-side automatic retry for 202 responses and instead rely on the webhook/callback from our service.
- Ensure the Idempotency-Key is preserved by any proxies/SDK layers between your client and our API.
- As a short-term platform mitigation we will add server-side deduplication for task_id + Idempotency-Key combos for 60s to prevent near-in-time duplicates. Config preview: `tooling.idempotency_window_seconds = 60` (hotfix rollout).

jamal_sre: Additional investigator notes: router trace shows an upstream LB retry due to a 502 on the initial connection attempt; LB retried the POST and the retried request lost the Idempotency-Key header when forwarded (known issue with that LB version). We'll coordinate with infra to patch that LB behavior.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0443 "duplicate-exec-via-lb-retry". Assigned to devon_platform and jamal_sre.

sara_support: Next steps for us: (1) billing ticket with proposed refund (if customer confirms), (2) dev to implement server dedupe and a short-term audit view showing duplicate execs per task_id, (3) infra to hotfix LB header preservation.

alice_finleaf: Thanks, team — we want the duplicate charge reversed if confirmed. We'll also run a repro in staging per your instructions. Here's a compact reproducible curl for you to test in staging (replace key + endpoint):
```
curl -i -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.example/v1/toolcall \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-staging' \\n  -H 'Idempotency-Key: test-dup-001' \\n  -d '{"tool":"charge_customer","args":{"customer_id":"CUST-TEST","amount":1.00}}'
```
Please let us know when the server dedupe is live and if you need more logs. :thumbsup:

devon_platform: We'll prioritize a hotfix and post back here with the rollout ETA and a follow-up verification checklist (staging repro, logs showing dedupe hit, and a monitor for duplicate-charge events).
